messages.subject: MDArray Integration
parts:
Hello,

So, as I said before, I´m not experienced in R, so I would appreciate if you could give me some advice on the integration of MDArray and Renjin from the point of view of functionality and interface.

So, let´s say I have an MDArray (or MDMatrix) and I can convert that to a R Matrix as described in the previous email.  Now, should I create an RMatrix class and add methods to this class?  Then I would probably need also a RDataSet class and other such R classes. 

Another approach would be to create a Renjin class and then "import" the MDArray to Renjin and from them on work inside Renjin sending to it strings to be interpreted.  I don´t really like this approach as the integration is very "thin". 

On the other hand, I also think that if we start with a data set in Renjin, how to make use of MDArray features? 

One of the things I´ve read many times is that programming in R is a real pain, so could MDArray/Renjin come up with a better model that allowed for programming in Ruby and geting all of R´s functionality?  For instance, it would be great if I could start with a large multidimensional array (in a NetCDF file), make a loop (in Ruby) that took views from this array, for each of those views find, say, a linear regression with Renjin, and the store the results in a Ruby array for printing and visualization.

Thanks for comments/advice.


Cheers,


Rodrigo
